summary: Resolves the a2-th filename from a linked list rooted at this+0x444, guarded by the element count at this+0x450. Bounds or walk failures return the byte_5EA438 fallback. On success the leaf string is copied into a stack/object buffer at this+836, truncated at the first '.' (extension), then the pointer is advanced past the last '\' so the result points at the bare filename.

operations.description: Bounds guard: return byte_5EA438 when a2 < 0 or a2 >= the element count at this+0x450.
Start the walk at the list head stored at this+0x444.
When a2 > 0, follow node next pointers at node+4 until a2 nodes have been skipped; if the list ends first, return byte_5EA438.
Guard: return byte_5EA438 if the reached node v4 is NULL or if the inner pointer stored at node+0 is NULL.
Dereference the leaf string pointer; when the string is empty use byte_5EA438 as the source instead.
Copy the resolved string into the buffer at this+836 via strcpy.
Scan backwards from the buffer end for the first '.' (0x2E) and null-terminate there, stripping the file extension; stop at the buffer base.
Scan backwards from the buffer end for the last '\\' (0x5C); return a pointer just past it, giving the bare filename. If none found, return the buffer start.
Return a pointer into the this+836 buffer: the bare filename after path/extension stripping, or byte_5EA438 on any failure.

unresolved: Buffer base at this+836 and element count/head offsets (this+0x450, this+0x444) belong to the owning object, which is unnamed; exact struct layout unknown.
